This is a fresh, complete English translation of Wu Cheng’en’s public-domain one-hundred-chapter novel, produced with GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark assistance. It is an AI-assisted first edition, not a reproduction of an existing translation.

So it was known that the Equal-to-Heaven Great Sage was, after all, only a demon monkey. No one even knew his official rank or stipend grade, and no one compared salaries with him; just naming him was enough. The two divisions of Immortal clerks under the Qi Tian Palace attended him morning and evening. He only knew to take three meals by day, sleep on one bed by night, and with no business to pull him in had complete freedom. In his spare time he met friends and roamed the palaces, making sworn friendships. He addressed the Three Purities with the honorific “Old,” and when he met the Four Emperors he addressed them as “Your Majesty.” With the Nine Luminaries, the Generals of the Five Directions, the Twenty-Eight Mansions, the Four Great Heavenly Kings, the Twelve Yuan stars, the Five-direction elders, the astrologers of all the heavens, and the River-and-Lake gods of He and Han, he treated them all as brothers. Today he traveled east, tomorrow west; drifting in and out of the clouds, his movements were unpredictable.

One day, at the Jade Emperor’s morning court, a true immortal named Xu Jingyang stepped forward and knelt to report, “Now the Great Sage of Equal-to-Heaven is free of duties and roams in idleness, making friends with all heavenly constellations regardless of rank and calling them all companions. I fear trouble may arise from his idle wandering. Better entrust him with some charge so trouble can be prevented.” Hearing this, the Jade Emperor issued an edict at once. The Monkey King came at once, smiling in happiness: “Your Majesty, what promotion or reward does the edict grant Old Monkey?” The Jade Emperor said, “I see you have free time and no task, so here is one assignment: for now, take charge of the Peach Garden and attend to it carefully.” The Great Sage was overjoyed, thanked him, bowed in court, and withdrew.

The moment he had no more pressing duties, he entered the Peach Garden to inspect it. Inside the garden a local Earth God blocked him and asked, “Where is Great Sage going?” The Great Sage said, “By the Jade Emperor’s order, I have been appointed to oversee the Peach Garden and have come to inspect it.” The Earth God quickly paid his respects and summoned the teams of tree-pruning attendants, water-drawing attendants, peach-maintenance attendants, and sweep attendants, all of whom bowed and led him in. There he saw:

Lush and brilliant, thick with bloom and fruit in every cluster, every bough crowded with ripe globes. Blossoms bloomed vivid along the trees, ripe fruits pressed down the branches. The fruits weighed down the boughs, hanging like hanging brocade tassels; blossoms on the trees clustered like rouge. Opened and closed by turns, each ripening took a thousand years; there was no summer and no winter, and ages passed slowly. The earliest ripe ones had cheeks flushed as red as wine; the later ones still bore green stems and greenish skins. Their smoldering flesh carried a green sheen, and in sunlight they showed their red-lacquer brilliance. Beneath them grew strange blossoms and strange herbs, and in all four seasons the colors did not fade. On both sides stood pavilions and halls, filling the sky, veiled by cloud and rainbow light. They were not grown from ordinary worldly seeds; the Queen Mother of the Jasper Pool had cultivated them herself.

After looking in delight for a long while, the Great Sage asked the Earth God, “How many trees are there in total?” The Earth God said, “There are three thousand six hundred: first, one thousand two hundred, with small blossoms and small fruits, ripening once every three thousand years; anyone who eats them becomes a transcendent, with a healthy body and light frame. In the middle, one thousand two hundred with layered blossoms and sweet flesh, ripening every six thousand years; whoever eats them rises skyward and never ages. At the back, one thousand two hundred with purple-veined kernels ripen every nine thousand years; whoever eats them attains lifespan equal to heaven and earth, living as long as the Sun and Moon.” The Great Sage heard this and rejoiced beyond measure. That day he checked over all the trees and pavilions and returned to his hall. From then on, every three to five days he came to enjoy himself, neither making friends with others nor going elsewhere.

One day he saw the old branches of one tree heavy with ripe peaches. He wished to taste something new, but the garden spirits and attendant spirits of the Great Heaven remained close and made it inconvenient. He devised a plan: "You all wait outside at the gate. Let me rest a while in this pavilion." They withdrew. The Monkey King removed crown and robes, climbed up the great tree, selected perfectly ripe peaches, and plucked many of them, then, lounging among the branches, ate to satiety. Only after he had eaten enough did he drop down, restored crown and robes, and called the attendants back and returned. Two or three days later he would try again, stealing peaches whenever he pleased.

One day the Queen Mother held a grand banquet and opened the treasure hall, making a triumphal Peach Assembly in the Waters of Jade. She ordered the Immortal Maidens in scarlet, blue, white, black, purple, yellow, and green robes to carry flower baskets and gather peaches from the Peach Garden for the feast. When the seven maids reached the garden gate, they found the garden spirit and its earth-guarding men there with the court attendants of the Great Heaven. As they bowed and reached the gate the maiden in lead said, "By the Queen Mother’s sacred order, we have come to harvest peaches and prepare the banquet." The earth spirit said, "Immortal ladies, please wait. This year is not as in past years. The Jade Emperor has commissioned the Great Sage of Equal-to-Heaven to supervise here, and I dare not open the grounds before reporting to him." A maiden said, "Where is the Great Sage?" The spirit said, "He is in the garden, napping in a pavilion from weariness." The maiden answered, "Then go find him at once; do not delay." The spirit and others entered with them. They searched the flower pavilion and found nothing but robes and capes there; he had vanished. He had only napped awhile after eating several peaches, then in monkey trickery had shrunk to the height of two inches and slept beneath dense leaves at the top of a high bough. The seven maidens said, "We came on command, yet we cannot find him. How can we return empty-handed?" A nearby immortal envoy spoke: "If your ladies have come under orders, do not hesitate. Our Great Sage is used to wandering. He has likely gone out to meet friends outside the garden. Go ahead and pick peaches; we will carry your words back."

The maidens did as told and entered the grove to pluck peaches: first two baskets from the front rows, three more from the middle, and then to the rear trees. At the back only a few pale green, fuzzy-stemmed peaches remained; all the ripe ones had been eaten. The seven looked everywhere and saw only one peach on a southern branch, half red, half white. The blue-robed maiden pulled a branch down, and the red-robed maiden plucked that peach and set the branch aside.

The Great Sage had in truth transformed himself and was sleeping there on that branch. He woke with a start, resumed his true form, drew out his golden staff from his ear, flourished it once—its girth swelled like a vessel—and said sharply, "Who are you, what monster dare to pluck my peaches?" The seven maidens, startled, knelt together. "Great Sage, calm yourself. We are no demons, but the seven robed maidens sent by the Queen Mother to gather immortals’ peaches for the banquet in the Hall of Treasures. We came and first saw the local earth spirit; he could not find the Great Sage. Fearing we might delay the Queen Mother’s command, we dare not wait and so began plucking. Please forgive this offense." Hearing her words, the Great Sage smiled and set aside his wrath. "Rise, Immortal ladies. For this feast in the Hall, whom have they invited?" The maidens answered, "By precedent, Buddha of the Western Heaven, bodhisattvas, saintly monks, and arhats are invited, along with Guanyin of the southern polar heavens, the august Dharma Emperor of the east and the Three Islets and Three Islands Immortal Elders, Xuanling of the north, Huang Jiao the Great Immortal of the central yellow extremity, and the Five elders of the five directions. There are also the lord of the Big Dipper stars, the Three Purities of the upper eight palaces, Four Emperors, Taiyi heavenly immortals above; the Jade Emperor’s retinue and the Nine-terrace hosts, mountain-and-sea spirits above; beneath them, lords of the nether palaces and sovereigns of the dark realms of the underworld, with principal and lesser deities from every court and hall—all in attendance." The Great Sage laughed, "Did they invite me?" The maidens said, "No word reached us." He replied, "I am the Equal-to-Heaven Great Sage. Why should it be improper to invite Old Son to preside at a seat? What is the harm?" They said, "This is the old rule for the Supreme Assembly; none knows if this gathering is arranged as before." The Great Sage said, "True. No wonder you do not know. Stand where you are. I will first go inquire whether I am indeed uninvited."

Greatly pleased, he muttered a formula, chanted a charm, and said to all the maidens, "Stop! Stop! Stop!" It was a sealing technique, freezing their limbs; each of the seven maidens stood beneath the peach tree with eyes wide open and unblinking, faces drained of color and unmoving. The Great Sage leapt like auspicious clouds and shot out of the garden straight toward the Jade Pool. As he went, a scene rose on the roadside:

A single day of omens and rosy light wavered,\n > five-hued auspicious clouds flew without cease.\n > The cry of white cranes rang through nine ravines,\n > purple-fungus blossoms gleamed like a thousand leaves.\n > In the center appeared one immortal, whose face and form held a natural, singular radiance.\n > Through rainbow-gleaming sky he danced a divine step,\n > a treasure register hung at his waist, free of birth and death.\n > His name: Chijiao Great Immortal,\n > come in person for the Feast of Added Longevity.

The bare-footed Great Immortal Chijiao met the Great Sage face to face. The Great Sage lowered his head and, on the spot, devised a ruse for a true immortal. He wished to slip through to the banquet unnoticed and yet asked, "Elder, where are you bound?" The Chijiao Sage replied, "The Queen Mother has summoned me to attend the Great Peach Assembly." The Great Sage answered, "You are not acquainted. The Jade Emperor, knowing Old Son can whirl clouds at speed, has sent him to summon all by five roads. One must first attend court before arriving at the Hall of Illumination, and only then go to the feast." The bare-footed one, a straightforward and upright man of light, accepted the stratagem as true and said, "But each year we render thanks for mercy in the Hall of Jasper Waters—how then can I first go to the Hall of Illumination and only afterward to the Peach banquet?" There was no help for it; he turned his omens-cloud and went directly to the Hall of Clear Brightness.

The Great Sage mounted his cloud, chanted a charm, changed form in a twinkle, and became the likeness of Chijiao Great Immortal, then rushed on toward the Jade Pool. Not long afterward he arrived at the treasure pavilion. He reined in the cloud-head, stepped down lightly, and walked inside. There he saw:

Pearly incense curled in fragrant spirals, auspicious vapors shimmered in wonder. The terraces of the jade realm were spread in colored streamers; the treasure hall drifted with gentle haze. Phoenixes rose and luans flew in elusive grace. Golden blossoms and jade cup-like blossoms floated and sank in wavering shadows. Above were arrayed canopies of nine-phae­nix vermilion-sun clouds, eight precious violet-rainbow pedestals, five-hued gold-leafed tables, and thousand-flower green-jade basins. On the tables were dragon liver and phoenix marrow, bear paws and ape lips. The banquet foods were a hundred delicacies, each excellent in flavor; strange fruits and festive dishes were fresh in every color.

Everything inside was arranged in perfect order and symmetry, yet no immortals had arrived.

That place was impeccably arranged, yet still no immortals had arrived.

The Great Sage looked around without seeing much, then suddenly caught a blast of wine aroma in his nostrils. Turning, he saw beneath the right-side corridor a few wine-making immortals, mash-stirring attendants, along with a few Daoist water carriers and fire-keeping boys who were scrubbing jars and tubs, already producing jade-like spirit and fine fragrant wine. The Great Sage could not keep his mouth from drooling. He wanted to eat, but all those people were right there. So he used a trick, plucked a few hair strands from his mane, chewed them to pieces in his mouth and blew them out, chanted a charm, and said, “Transform!” They at once became dozing bugs that flew onto everyone’s faces. Look at that crowd: their hands went limp, heads drooped, brows lowered, eyes closed together; they dropped their duties and all went off to sleep. The Great Sage then took a number of the hundred-flavored and eight-precious dishes, and other fine and strange foods, entered the corridor, went from vat to jar, drank to his fill, and caroused for some time. He drank heavily and became drunk. He thought to himself, “This is bad, bad! The invited guests will arrive in a bit—will they not blame me? If they catch me at once, what am I to do? Better to go back to my own hall and sleep right away.”

The Great Sage swayed and leaned on the wine, recklessly colliding as he pleased. In a moment he missed the way: it was not the Qitian Hall but the Hall of Doushaì. He suddenly cleared-headed and said, “The Doushàí Palace is above the Thirty-Three Heavens, the seat of the Supreme Lord Lao in the Heaven of Departed Grief; how did I end up here by mistake? All right then, all right then—I've long meant to come and have seen this old master, but never had the chance. Since I have this leftover misstep, I may as well look on him once.” He adjusted his clothes and barged in, but there he saw no Old Lord, not a trace of anyone.

In truth, that old master and the Buddha of Luminous Lamp were giving a sermon on a three-tiered high tower atop the cinnabar altar. Immortal boys, immortal generals, immortal officials, and immortal clerks stood on both sides listening. The Great Sage went straight into the alchemical chamber and searched, but found no one. Beside the furnace were five gourds, and in each were already-refined golden pills. The Great Sage said in joy, “This is the highest treasure of immortals. Since I learned the Way, I have understood that internal and external are one, yet I too wish to refine some golden elixirs to benefit people, though there was no time for it at home. Today I have this good fortune and yet have run into this thing by chance. While the old master is away, let me eat a few pills and taste the new.” He poured every one of the gourds out and ate them all, just like munching roasted beans.

In an instant he fully sobered up. He thought to himself, “No, no! This calamity is bigger than heaven; if I alarm the Jade Emperor, my life may not be spared. Leave, leave—better go down below and become king.” He ran out of Doushì Palace, did not take the old path, and escaped through the Western Heavenly Gate by using a concealment method. Then he pressed the cloud-head and returned to the border of Flower-Fruit Mountain. There he saw flashing banners and radiant halberds: it was the Four Marshals and the Seven-Two Hundred? Actually no, the Seven-Two? [corrected] the 72 Caves monsters’ kings there practicing martial arts. The Great Sage shouted, “You youngsters, I am here!” The monsters cast down their weapons and knelt, saying, “Great Sage, have peace of mind; we have been left for a long time and feared you had forgotten to attend to us.” The Great Sage said, “Not long now, not long.”

Then he marched on straight into the deep caverns. The four marshals set matters in order and, after bowing and paying respects, all said, “Great Sage, during the hundred and ten years in Heaven, what post did you actually hold?” The Great Sage laughed, “It feels like only half a year to me—how can you say a hundred and ten years?” The marshal replied, “One day in Heaven is a year below.” The Great Sage said, “As for this, the Jade Emperor has favored me: he bestowed upon me the title Great Sage, Equal to Heaven; raised a Great Heavenly Office; and set up the Offices of Tranquility and Pacification with immortal attendants and guards. Later, seeing I had nothing to do, he made me supervise the Peach Garden. Recently the Queen Mother held a Peach Banquet and did not invite me. I did not wait for her invitation, I first went to the Jade Pool and stole and ate all his divine food and divine wine. Leaving the Jade Pool, staggering, I accidentally entered Lord Lao’s palace and also ate his five gourd-golden elixirs. But fearing the Jade Emperor would discover my crime, I just now left through the Heavenly Gate.”

The monsters rejoiced on hearing this. They arranged wine and fruit to welcome him, and presented a stone cup filled to the brim with coconut wine. The Great Sage took one sip and said, “Not good, not good.” The two marshals Beng and Ba replied, “Great Sage has tasted immortal wine and immortal fare in Heaven, so coconut wine seems inferior in taste. As the saying goes: ‘No matter how good, it is the water of one’s native place.’” The Great Sage said, “You’re all ‘close or not, it’s still people from one’s native place.’ Earlier today while I was reveling in the Jade Pool, I saw many jars beneath the long corridor, all containing jade-like spirit nectar. None of you have tasted it. Let me go steal a few more to bring back; each of you drink just half a cup and you’ll all live long without aging or death.” The monkeys rejoiced beyond measure.

The Great Sage came out through the cave gate again, chanted a spell and turned the cloud-head, then went straight to the Peach Banquet at the Jade Pool palace. There he saw those handling winemaking, mash, water carrying, and fire tending still fast asleep, snoring. He snatched two by their sides under the arms, took two in each hand, then turned the cloud-head and returned. Back in the cave with the assembled monkeys, they held a heavenly wine gathering; each drank a few cups, and all were joyful—no need to elaborate.

As for the seven-robed fairies, they were held by the Great Sage’s fixed-body spell and could be released only after one heavenly cycle. Each carrying a flower basket, they returned and reported to the Queen Mother: “The Great Sage, Equal to Heaven, used his spell to restrain us, and for this reason we arrived late.” The Queen Mother asked, “How many peaches did you pick?” The maidens answered, “Only two baskets of small peaches and three baskets of medium peaches. As for the back rows, not even half a big peach remains—surely the Great Sage must have eaten them. While I was searching, suddenly he came out and began to beat and terrorize us, and then asked who was invited to host the banquet. We explained everything of the hall’s occasion; he then fixed and held us, and we did not know where he had gone. Only now are we able to wake and return.”

The Queen Mother heard this and immediately went to see the Jade Emperor, laying out all that had transpired. She had not yet finished when those who had made the wine together with the attending immortals came in to report: “We do not know who it was, but that fellow disrupted the banquet of the Peaches, stole heavenly wine, and stole all the eight precious flavors as well.” Then four Great Celestial Masters arrived to report: “The Most High Patriarch of the Way has come.” The Jade Emperor and the Queen Mother went out to receive him. After completing his ceremonial bows, Laojun said, “I have refined a batch of nine-revolutionary Golden Pill Elixir in the Great Palace for Your Majesty’s Great Assembly of Vital Essence. I never thought some thief would steal it away. I now bring this to your attention.” The Jade Emperor was alarmed. Presently another heavenly officer from the Qitian Office knelt and said, “The Great Sage Sun Wukong did not keep to his duties; since yesterday he went out on an outing and has not yet returned, and his whereabouts are unknown.” The Jade Emperor grew even more suspicious. Again the Barefoot Great Immortal came in and reported: “By the Queen Mother’s command, I attended yesterday’s assembly. There I happened to meet the Great Sage of Equal to Heaven. He told me that the Emperor had commanded him to summon me and others first to the Hall of Bright Clarity to perform ritual bows, and only then to attend the meeting. I followed his words, returned to the Hall’s outside gate, and when I did not see the august dragon carriage or phoenix sedan, I hurried back here and waited.” The Jade Emperor cried out in greater astonishment, “This rogue forged the command and duped the august ministers. Hurry and order the Celestial Inspector of Spirits to pursue his trail.”

Taking command, the Spiritual Officer set out from the hall, searched everywhere, and reported every detail: it was indeed the Great Sage of Equal to Heaven who had thrown Heaven into uproar. He recounted the earlier events once more. The Jade Emperor grew furious and dispatched the Four Great Heavenly Kings together with Li Tianwang and Prince Nezha, ordering the Twenty-Eight Stellar Officers, the Nine Luminaries, the Twelve Primordial Deities, the Five Directional Overseers, the Four Duty Censors, the Star Formations of East and West, the Two Divine Guardians of North and South, the Five Mountains and Four Rivers, and the entire heavenly star host—one hundred thousand celestial soldiers in all—to lay eighteen arrays of heavenly nets and earthbound snares, descend to the lower world, and encircle Flower-Fruit Mountain to seize that rogue and bring him to judgment.

All the gods immediately raised their ranks and left the Heavenly Palace. As they set out, they saw this:

Yellow winds churned and rolled, blackening the sky; purple mists surged up, darkening the earth. Only because a demon monkey dared to affront the Son of Heaven, it drove all the sages down to the mortal world. Four Great Heavenly Kings and the Five Great Yedi: the four kings assumed command, and the Five Great Yedi arranged many troops. Li, the Banner-Pole Tuo General, was the center commander and front signal-keeper, while fierce Nezha led the vanguard. Luo-hou star served as the lead inspector, with Jiedu star pressing behind in towering force. Taiyin’s spirit was braced and alert, and Taiyang shone clearly in its brilliance. The Five-Element stars were especially brave and imposing; the Nine Luminaries most liked to contend. For YUANCHEN, the Zi, Wu, Mao, and You hours, one and all were mighty heavenly guards. The Five Plagues and Five Peaks were set out east and west; the Six Ding and Six Jia moved on both sides. The Four-Fold Mouth Dragon Gods held upper and lower positions; the Twenty-Eight Mansions were arrayed in dense layers. The stars Jiao, Kang, Di, and Fang were in overall command; Kui, Lou, Wei, and Mao kept their steeds in restless motion. Dipper, Ox, Woman, Void, Wei, and Bi (the wall-star cluster) each showed prowess. The Well, Gui, Liu, and star Zhang Yi with Ji Yin handled the spears and swirled their swords, showing fearsome spirit and power. Stopping-cloud and descending-mist entered the mortal world; in front of Flower-Fruit Mountain they pitched camp. Poem: Heaven-born monkey king shifts forms in endless ways, stealing elixirs and wine to revel in his rocky den. It is only because he disrupted the Peach Banquet that ten-thousand ranks of heavenly soldiers spread their snares.

At that time, Li Tianwang issued orders and directed all the heavenly troops to set up camp, enclosing Flower-Fruit Mountain so tightly that not even water could pass through. They laid the eighteenth array of heavenly and earth nets above and below, then first sent out the Nine Bad Stars to engage. The Nine Luminaries, bearing troops, marched straight to the cave mouth and saw only groups of monkeys outside and inside the cave leaping and frolicking. The star marshal shouted in a hard voice, “You little demon, where is your Great Sage? We are heavenly generals dispatched from the upper realms to bring down this rebel Great Sage. Let him surrender at once. If he refuses even one word, all of you will be exterminated.” The little monkey hurried in to report, “Great Sage, disaster! Disaster! Outside there are nine ferocious gods, claiming they are heavenly deities sent from above to take you in.”

At that moment, the Great Sage was sharing immortal wine with the seventy-two cave demon kings and four top commanders. On hearing this report, he deliberately ignored it and said, “Drink today and be drunk today—don’t concern yourself with right or wrong at the gate.” He had not finished speaking when another little demon came bounding in: “That line nine fierce stars are hurling coarse abuses and shouting for battle at the gate.” The Great Sage laughed, “Ignore them. Let wine and verse matter for today’s joy; no matter when fame comes.” Before he could finish, yet another little demon arrived: “Master! Those nine ferocious stars have broken the gate and are barging in.” The Great Sage grew angry: “These bald, coarse-haired gods are terribly rude. I had meant to make no calculations with them, yet how dare they come to our gate to bully me?” He ordered the Horned Ghost King: “Lead out the seventy-two cave demon kings to battle. Great Sun Wukong, follow with the four bodyguards.” That king quickly rushed forth leading the demon soldiers to meet them, but the nine evil stars converged and attacked together; they were held at the bridge of the Iron Slab, and could not break through.

In the uproar, the Great Sage arrived. He cried, “Open the way!” pulled free his iron staff, and with one sweep, broad as a bowl and two zhang long, he tossed it from its stand and stepped out fighting. None of those nine luminary stars dared to stand against him; he drove them back at once. The Nine Luminary stars held their formation and said, “You, oblivious to life and death, you Bima Wen, have committed the Ten Great Sins: first you stole peaches, then stole wine, disrupted the Peach Banquet, stole Laojun’s Immortal Elixir, and even stole the imperial wine to feast here in pleasure. Your crimes are piled upon crimes—did you not know?” The Great Sage laughed, “Those few matters are real. But what is your point now?” One of the nine stars replied, “I bear the Jade Emperor’s golden edict. I have led all these troops here to arrest you. Surrender quickly so these living creatures may keep their lives; otherwise I will level this mountain and flip over this cave.” The Great Sage grew furious: “How can these hairy gods dare such words with so little power? Stand still and taste old-sun a single staff!” The nine stars surged together at once; the Beautiful Monkey King did not tremble in the slightest. He raised the Golden-hooped staff, shielding left and right. He fought the Nine Luminaries until their strength failed and their muscles grew weary; each of them dropped his weapons and retreated, broken in battle. They rushed into the central command tent and told the Tuo-Ta Heavenly King, “That monkey king is truly extremely valiant. We cannot beat him—this is a defeated engagement.”

Li Tianwang then summoned the Four Great Heavenly Kings and the Twenty-Eight Constellations and led out the troops to fight. The Great Sage showed no fear at all; he also called out the Horned Ghost King, the seventy-two cave demon kings, and four commanders, and set them in formation outside the cave mouth. Behold the melee—it was truly terrifying:

The cold wind whistled sharply; strange mists lay low. On one side banners of color streamed; on the other side halberds and spears blazed. Helmets rolled and shone in waves, armor shone in rank upon rank. Those rolling helmets flashing before the sun were like silver chimes crashing into heaven; layered armor rose like cliffs and ice mountains pressing the earth. The great pole-arms were like cloud-splitting lightning; the pale spears cut through fog and cloud. The Fangtian halberd, Tiger-Eye whip, and Maling array; bronze swords, Siming spades, ranks packed like thick forest. Curved bows, hard crossbows, carved-plume arrows, short clubs, and serpent spears, each ready to seize the soul. The Great Sage’s one Ruyi staff spun and flipped as he battled the heavenly gods. He struck so hard that no birds crossed the sky; in the mountain tigers and wolves ran in panic. Sand flew up, stones rolled, heaven and earth darkened, dust rose into soil and earth, and the universe seemed dim. One heard weapons clashing and thundering, terrifying cries that shook gods and spirits.

This battle took up its array from the hour of the dragon until sunset in the west. The Horned Ghost King and the seventy-two cave demons were all taken by the heavenly gods. Only the four commanders and that troop of monkeys were spared and hid deep at the bottom of the water-screen cave.

With that one Ruyi staff, the Great Sage blocked the Four Great Heavenly Kings, Li Tuota, and Prince Nezha, all in midair, and fought for a long while. As dusk approached, he plucked a tuft of hair, put it in his mouth, chewed it to pieces, spat it out, and shouted, “Transform!” Immediately he became hundreds upon hundreds of Great Sages, each wielding the Ruyi staff, drove back Nezha, and put five heavenly kings to flight.

The Great Sage, victorious, gathered his hair, turned, and hurried back to the cave. He soon saw the four commanders and all the troops kneeling at the Iron-Plate Bridge. The crowd sobbed out three times and then laughed three times in loud, broken gasps. The Great Sage said, “Now that you have seen me, why both crying and laughing?” The four commanders said, “This morning we led troops and fought the Heavenly King; the seventy-two cave demon kings and the Horned Ghost King were all taken by the heavenly gods. We survived by escaping, so this is why we should cry. Now that we see the Great Sage has returned victorious and unhurt, this is why we should laugh.” The Great Sage said, “Victory and defeat are the way of war. The ancients said, ‘Kill ten thousand, lose three thousand.’ As for the chiefs who were captured, they were of the sort tiger, leopard, wolf, insects and vermin, badger, broad-hoofed antelope, fox, and raccoon-dog. Not one of our own kind was harmed. Why should there be anxiety? Though I drove him back with my division-duplicate art, he still intends to camp at the foot of my mountain. We should hold firmly, eat our fill once, sleep securely, and restore strength. At dawn I will show a great divine art, seize these heavenly generals, and take revenge with all.” The four commanders and the monkey chiefs drank a few bowls of coconut wine, slept peacefully, and the matter is not told further.

The Four Great Heavenly Kings then stood down from battle. Each reported his achievements: one said he had caught a tiger or leopard, one said a lion or elephant, one said a wolf-creature or raccoon-like beast. Not one monkey spirit had been captured at all. At that time they set up a main encampment and a large field camp again, rewarded the deserving commanders, and sent out the troops of the celestial-earthly net, each soldier carrying a hand-bell and shouting orders to surround Flower-Fruit Mountain, waiting for battle at first light. Once ordered, each station stood guard in every place. It says:

When the wild monkey did mayhem, heaven and earth were shocked; nets were laid and watch kept by night and day.

How they dealt with the matter after daybreak, we shall have resolved in the next installment.
chapters.title: Chapter 5: The Great Sage stirs chaos in the Peach Garden and steals the elixir; he rebellions in Heaven while the gods seek to seize the demon.

This is a fresh, complete English translation of Wu Cheng’en’s public-domain one-hundred-chapter novel, produced with GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark assistance. It is an AI-assisted first edition, not a reproduction of an existing translation.

There is no need to speak of how heavenly gods crowded around; the Great Sage came to rest. The Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva of Great Compassion and Great Mercy who dwelt on Mount Lao-jia of Putuo in the South Sea, having been invited by the Queen Mother of the West to attend the Peach Banquet in the Hall of Great Splendor, had gone there together with her senior disciple, the Monk Hui'an, and in that same crystal pavilion they beheld desolation, shattered seats and scattered offerings. Although a few heavenly immortals were present, none had taken their places; all argued restlessly in confusion. After meeting the Bodhisattva and all the immortals, they recounted all that had transpired. Guanyin said, “When the feast is not truly in session and no cups are being passed, you should follow this humble monk and go meet the Jade Emperor.” The immortals, all in good spirits, followed. At the gate of the Hall of Radiant Clarity, four Great Heavenly Masters and Chi-jiao Celestial Immortals were already waiting, greeting Guanyin. They explained that the Jade Emperor was troubled: the celestial troops had been dispatched and monsters had been seized, but had not yet been brought back. Guanyin said, “I need to see the Jade Emperor and convey your difficulties.” Qiuhongji, the Great Master, entered the Lingxiao Treasure Hall and announced her arrival. There sat the Supreme Patriarch Lao Jun and behind him the Queen Mother of the West.

Guanyin led the company inside and paid respects to the Jade Emperor, then bowed to Laojun and the Queen Mother, and all took their seats. She asked, “How has the Peach Banquet gone?” The Jade Emperor replied, “Every year we hold it in joy and celebration; this year, because that demon monkey wreaked havoc, it is only an empty invitation.” Guanyin asked, “Where does this demon-monkey come from?” The Jade Emperor answered, “That demon was born from a stone egg on Flower-Fruit Mountain in Aulai of the Eastern Victory Continent. When he was born, his eyes cast out golden light that shot toward the Dipper. At first we paid him no heed. Later he became an adept, subdued dragons and tigers and slew lives at will. When the Dragon King and King Yama submitted reports, I wished to arrest him. It was then that Changeng Star reported: ‘Among the Three Realms, anyone with nine orifices may become an immortal.’ So I taught and instructed him, summoned him up, and made him official in charge of the Jade Horses, a Bima-wun post. He disliked the lowly office and rebelled against Heaven. I then ordered Li Tianwang and Prince Nezha to subdue him; and after issuing an edict of pacification and bringing him up to Heaven, I conferred on him the title Great Sage Equal to Heaven, but with office and no salary. Because he had nothing to do, he roamed east and west. Fearing he would cause trouble, I made him supervise the Peach Garden. He disobeyed the law, devoured all the old-fruiting peaches. When the banquet was arranged he was not among the summoned officials and was not invited. He deceived Chi-jiao Immortal, changed his form and slipped in, then stole all celestial food and wine, stole Laojun’s divine pills, and stole some court wine, and took them back to share with the monkeys on his own mountain. I was vexed, so I deployed ten thousand, no, ten thousand? heavenly soldiers with Heaven-net and Earth-net to capture him. A day has now passed and no troops have returned; the outcome is still unknown.” Guanyin, hearing this, told Hui’an, “Go quickly down to Flower-Fruit Mountain and scout the situation. If you meet him in battle, render one helping hand; make sure you return with a true report.”

Hui’an adjusted his robe and took up an iron cudgel, mounted a cloud, and went straight to the mountain front. He saw the Heaven-Net and Earth-Net layered thick and close, each camp gate with bells and cries; the mountain was enclosed so tightly that nothing could pass through. Hui’an halted and called out, “Tell the camp officers at the gates: I am Mutcha, second prince of Li Tianwang, Hui’an, the Great Disciple of Guanyin of the South Sea, and I have come specifically to scout the military situation.” At once those guards relayed it to the main command tent. Already there were Xu-ri Mouse, Mao-ri Cock, Xing-ri Horse, and Fang-ri Rabbit reporting it to the central camp. Li Tianwang raised a command banner and ordered the Heaven-Net and Earth-Net opened to admit him. At that dawn in the east, Hui’an entered with the banner and saw Li Tianwang and the Four Great Heavenly Kings, and he bowed to them. After the bow, Li Tianwang said, “Boy, from where do you come?” Hui’an replied, “This fool followed the Bodhisattva to the Peach Banquet. The Bodhisattva found the assembly place desolate and the Jade Pool empty, so she took all the immortals and this fool to see the Jade Emperor. The Jade Emperor said you were sent below to subdue the demon monkey and in a day had no report returned, outcome unknown, so he asked me to probe the truth.” Li Tianwang said, “We camped here only yesterday and set up camp here. I sent the Nine Luminaries to challenge him; this brute used wondrous powers and all Nine Stars were defeated and returned. Later, when we personally brought troops, he scattered our formation. Our ten thousand? actually ten thousand? soldiers and he fought us in mixed combat till dusk; he used a multiplicity-of-bodies method and drove us back. When we later gathered the troops and searched, we only caught a few wolves, insects, tigers, and leopards; not one monkey demon was taken. We have not yet gone out to fight today.

He had barely finished when someone came from outside the gate with the report: “That Great Sage has brought a band of monkey demons and is calling for battle outside.” The Four Great Heavenly Kings, Li Tianwang, and the prince were in the middle of deliberating dispatching troops when Mutcha spoke: “Father, this poor novice, by Guanyin’s instruction, came down to scout and report. If there is battle, I should be able to help. I am not afraid now; let me go and see what kind of Great Sage he is.” Li Tianwang said, “Child, since you have trained under the Bodhisattva these years, you surely have acquired some divine arts. Be careful.”

The fine prince, with both hands brandishing his iron cudgel, knotted his embroidered robe and sprang from the gate, crying aloud, “Which is the Great Sage Equal to Heaven?” The Great Sage raised his Ruyi staff and shouted back, “It is Old Monkey. Who are you to dare ask me such a thing?” Mutcha said, “I am Mutcha, the second son of Li Tianwang, now at Guanyin’s seat serving as a disciple-protector. My Dharma name is Hui’an.” The Great Sage said, “You are not even training in the South Sea—why have you come here to face me?” Mutcha said, “My master sent me to inspect the battle. Seeing you so rampant, I have come to capture you.” The Great Sage said, “You dare speak such vain words. Do not run; take this one blow from Old Monkey.” Mutcha was not afraid at all, and swung his iron staff in a cross-handed welcome. The two stood in the midst of the slope outside the gate and the battle was fierce:

棍雖對棍鐵各異，兵縱交兵人不同。一個是太乙散仙呼大聖，一個是觀音徒弟正元龍。 渾鐵棍乃千鎚打，六丁六甲運神功；如意棒是天河定，鎮海神珍法力洪。 兩個相逢真對手，往來解數實無窮。這個的陰手棍萬千兇，繞腰貫索疾如風；那個的夾槍棒不放空，左遮右擋怎相容。 那陣上旌旗閃閃，這陣上鼉鼓鼕鼕。萬員天將團團繞，一洞妖猴簇簇叢。怪霧愁雲漫地府，狼煙煞氣射天宮。昨朝混戰還猶可，今日爭持更又兇。堪羨猴王真本事，木叉復敗又逃生。

The Great Sage and Hui’an fought five or six rounds. Hui’an’s arms became numb and weak; he could not withstand him, gave a false feint, and withdrew from the field in defeat. The Great Sage then withdrew his monkey troops and stationed them outside the cave mouth. At Li Tianwang’s camp gate, great and small heavenly soldiers seized the prince, parted the way, and let him pass straight through the gate. He spoke rapidly, out of breath, to the Four Heavenly Kings, Li Tuo-ta, and Nezha: “Great Sage! Great Sage! His powers are truly vast. I, your son, could not beat him and had to retreat defeated.” Li Tianwang was startled; he immediately ordered a memorial to be written and dispatched Great-Strength Ghost King and Prince Muzha to petition Heaven.

The two did not dare linger. They broke through the Heaven-and-Earth net, then mounted auspicious, radiant clouds and mists. Soon they reached beneath the Hall of Brilliant Clarity, saw the Four Great Heavenly Masters, and were led to the Lingxiao Treasure Hall to submit the memorial. Hui’an also paid homage to the Bodhisattva. Guanyin asked, “How did your scouting go?” Hui’an replied, “As first commanded, I came to Flower-Fruit Mountain and had the heaven-and-earth net gate opened. I saw Father, and he said, ‘Yesterday I fought that monkey king once; only tiger, leopard, lion, and elephant spirits were captured, not a single monkey spirit. While speaking, he challenged again. I, a disciple, fought him with an iron staff for five or six dozen bouts and could not win, then withdrew in defeat.’ So Father sent Great-Strength Ghost King and me to seek help above.” Guanyin lowered her head in thought.

The Jade Emperor opened the memorial and, on seeing the plea for help, laughed: “How dare this monkey demon be so skillful as to stand against ten thousand heavenly soldiers? Li Tianwang has come for help again—are the road gods and heavenly troops really expected to aid him?” Before he finished, Guanyin joined her palms and spoke: “Your Majesty, do not be troubled. This poor monk can name one divine lord who can capture that monkey.” The Jade Emperor asked, “Which god do you name?” Guanyin replied, “It is Your Majesty’s nephew, the Manifest Sage Erlang Zhenjun, who dwells in Guanzhou, at the mouth of the Gan River, receiving incense from below. In former days he completely subdued six demons, and he has with him the six Meishan brothers and twelve-hundred Grass-Head gods before his gate; his powers are vast. Yet he only obeys command-and-support summons, not proclamations. If Your Majesty issues a mobilization order, he can be sent to aid and he will surely seize this monkey.” The Jade Emperor, on hearing this, issued a mobilization edict and ordered Great-Strength Ghost King to carry it.

The ghost king took the decree, mounted the clouds, and went straight to the Ganjiang mouth, reaching the true lord’s temple in less than half an hour. The ghost sentinel at the gate had already reported, “A heavenly envoy is here with the court decree.” Erlang came out with his brothers to receive the envoy, burned incense, and read it. The decree stated:

On Flower-Fruit Mountain the demonic monkey, Great Sage Equal to Heaven, has rebelled. He stole peaches, wine, and elixirs from Heaven, disturbed the Peach-Peak banquet; though ten thousand heavenly soldiers and eighteen layers of heaven-and-earth net were deployed to encircle the mountain and capture him, he has not been taken. Therefore dispatch Your Majesty’s favored nephew and his sworn brothers at once to Flower-Fruit Mountain to suppress him. Great reward awaits after success. Hearing this, the True Lord rejoiced: “Have the envoy return. I will go at once with sword in hand to aid.” The ghost king returned with his report; no further matter is recorded.

The True Lord then summoned the six elder brothers of Meishan—Kang, Zhang, Yao, and Li—and the two generals Guo Shen and Zhijian, gathering them before the hall: “Just now the Jade Emperor has dispatched us to Flower-Fruit Mountain to capture this demonic monkey. Let us go together.” All brothers gladly agreed. He then ordered his own divine troops, mounted on eagles and dogs, prepared crossbows and strings, and, as violent wind raged, in an instant crossed the Eastern Ocean and went straight to Flower-Fruit Mountain. Seeing the heaven-and-earth net in dense layers that blocked advance, he called out to the net’s divine commanders: “I am Erlang, the Manifest Sage True Lord, sent by the Jade Emperor to capture the monkey demon. Open the camp gates and let us pass.” The command was relayed layer by layer all at once. The Four Heavenly Kings and Li Tianwang came out through the gate to meet him. After courteous greeting, they inquired about the battle; Li Wang related what had happened. Erlang laughed and said, “As I have arrived, I must fight him through transformation. Do not cover the top with the heaven-and-earth net; close it only tightly around all four sides, and let me wrestle him. If I lose to him, you need not help—you will see my brothers support me. If I win, you need not bind him—you will see my brothers act. Ask only Li Tuo-ta to use a demon-shedding mirror and hold it in the air. Should he at some point be defeated and break away in flight, you must illuminate him clearly so he cannot escape.” The kings each took their positions in the four directions, and all heavenly troops took their battle stations.

Erlang then led out the four marshals, the two generals, and his seven brothers to challenge from camp. He ordered all commanders to guard the encampment and round up all eagle-and-dog troops. The Grass-Head gods obeyed. Erlang came only as far as outside the Water-Curtain Cave and saw the monkeys in strict ranks, arrayed in a coiled-dragon formation. In the center stood one pole banner inscribed with four characters: “Great Sage Equal to Heaven.” Erlang said, “That unruly demon—how can he claim the office of Great Sage Equal to Heaven?” The six brothers of Meishan said, “Stop admiring him; call him out to fight.” A sentry monkey at the camp mouth saw Erlang and ran in panic to report. The Monkey King then snatched up his golden-hooped staff, donned his gold armor, stepped into cloud sandals, tapped his purple-gold crown, sprang through the gate, and opened his eyes wide to look. The True Lord’s appearance was truly unusual, both refined and elegant. In truth, he was:

His appearance was handsome and clear; his appearance noble, shoulders with drooping ears, eyes shining bright. He wore a Three-Mountain flying-phoenix cap, and a robe of pale duck-goose-yellow. Golden-threaded boots with coiled-dragon socks, and a jewel belt adorned with eight precious blossoms. At his waist hung a crossbow of a new-moon form; in hand he held a three-cornered, two-edged spear. With an axe he cleft Peach Mountain, once saving his mother. A single shot struck down the Shanluo pair of phoenixes. Renowned in distant lands for crushing the Eight Demons; bound in righteousness with the seven holy ones of Meishan. Proud in spirit, he would not acknowledge Heaven’s protection; proud by nature, he returns to live as a deity at Guanjuan. Red-Cloud, luminous, efficacious holy spirit-saint; infinitely manifest, he is called Erlang.

The Great Sage saw him and with a laugh lifted up the Gold-Crowned Cudgel and cried out, “What minor general are you that dares to challenge me here so boldly?” The True Lord shouted back, “You blind brute, you cannot recognize me? I am the nephew of the Jade Emperor, the conferred Zhaohui Lingxian, Second Earl Erlang. By Heaven’s order I have come to seize you, this Bimawen monkey that has rebelled against the heavenly court. You still do not know life and death.” The Great Sage said, “I remember when the Jade Emperor’s sister descended as a mortal woman and, with Lord Yang, bore a son who split Peach Mountain with an axe. Is that you? I meant to curse you a bit, though I have no real grudge; I was about to strike you once with my staff—what a pity it would be to take your life. You little lordling, be quick and send for your Four Great Heavenly Kings!” The True Lord in rage said, “Vile monkey, stop your insolence! Take one slash from me!” The Great Sage sidestepped and in one motion swung back with the golden staff. The two now fought fiercely:

Zhaohui Erlang God and Sun Wukong, the Great Sage Equal to Heaven. This one, proud and deriding the enemy, was that handsome Monkey King; that one, unknown-faced, pressed to subdue him. As the two first met, both were eager for battle. They had never known shallow and deep before; today each learned which was light and which was heavy. The iron bars raced like leaping dragons, the divine blades whirled like dancing phoenixes. Left blocked, right attacked; charges forward and retreat met eye to eye. On one side, Meishan’s six younger brothers raised the wind to stir support; on the other, Ma-Liu’s four generals passed down the commands. Banners waved, drums boomed in unison, shouts and gongs all lent their support. The two swords and iron rods saw their chance and went and returned with no gap between one movement and the next. The Ruyi golden cudgel is a treasure of the seas, whose transformations can fly and soar and win the fight. If your body lags, your life should already be forfeit; once you misstep, you will trip and fall.

The True Lord and the Great Sage fought for more than three hundred rounds with no clear victor. Then the True Lord mustered his divine power and changed form, growing ten thousand zhang tall. He raised in both hands a three-pronged, double-bladed divine weapon; his face was blue, with protruding fangs and vermilion hair, fierce and wrathful, and he came straight at the Great Sage to cut off his head. The Great Sage also used his art and transformed to match Erlang’s build, with face and form the same. He raised one Ruyi golden cudgel, which at once became the pillar upholding heaven atop Mount Kunlun, blocking the Erlang God. This made the horse marshal and Liuyang Marshal tremble so they could scarcely stir the banner; even Bēng and Bā, the two officers, were timid and could not wield their swords and blades. In that formation, Kang, Zhang, Yao, Li, Guo-shen, and Zhijian relayed commands, releasing the Grass-Head gods. They drove out hawks and hounds from beyond Water Curtain Cave, set crossbows and drew bows, and together closed in for the kill. Sadly, the monkey troops and four valiant commanders were thrown into confusion, and two or three thousand spirits were taken. Those monkeys cast away spears and armor, flung down swords and spears, some ran, some shouted, some fled uphill, some returned to the cave. It was like nocturnal birds startled at their roosts, scattering across the sky like stars. The triumph of the brothers need not be detailed.

But as the True Lord and the Great Sage changed and fought in forms spanning Heaven and Earth, in the midst of the duel the Great Sage suddenly saw the demons in his own camp scattered in alarm and, sensing panic in himself, folded up his spell-forms, snatched his staff, and took to flight. Seeing him run, the True Lord came after him quickly: “Where do you think you’re going? Surrender at once and I will spare your life.” The Great Sage did not linger in battle and ran on. Near the mouth of the cave he ran straight into the four Great Commanders Kang, Zhang, Yao, and Li, along with generals Guo-shen and Zhijian, who together led their men to block the way, shouting, “Vile monkey! Where are you going?” Startled and flustered, he pinched the staff into a brocade needle and hid it in his ear. In an instant he changed form into a sparrow, perched and stuck at the top of a tree. The six brothers, in a panic, searched front and back and could not find him, and together called out, “The monkey spirit has run away! The monkey spirit has run away!”

At that point, true lord arrived and asked, “Brothers, where did he go? He vanished over there, didn’t he?” The other gods replied, “He was only encircled right here and then disappeared.” Erlang opened his fierce hawk-like eyes and saw the Great Sage transformed into a sparrow, nailed to a tree. He withdrew his true form, cast aside the divine spear, and unstrung his sling. Then he changed at once into a hawk-eagle, flapped out his wings, and flew to strike. The Great Sage saw this and with a sharp rush of wind on one wing shot up and turned into a great cī-lǎo-like bird, rising into the sky. Erlang saw him, hurriedly shook out his plumage, and changed into a great sea-crane, diving up through the clouds like a spear. The Great Sage then sank down, entered the ravine, and became a fish, plunging into the water. Erlang came to the ravine’s edge but saw no trace. In his heart he thought, “This monkey-god surely went into the water and must have changed into fish or shrimp. I’ll change again and seize him.” As sure as thought, he changed into a fish-eagle, drifting over the head of the descending current, waiting a while. The Great Sage, as a fish, was swimming with the current when he saw a flying bird: like a blue hawk, but no blue feathering; like a heron, but no plume on top; like an old stork, but no red legs. “It must be Erlang changing in order to meet me!” he quickly turned his head and, with a flick, took off. Erlang saw this and said, “That fish-like trickster: like a carp, but no red tail; like a bream, no spotted scales; like a catfish, no star on the head; like a sparid, no needles on the gills. Why did he turn back the moment he saw me? It must be that monkey’s transformation.” He charged forward and pecked one beakful. The Great Sage suddenly sprang from the water and changed into a water snake, swimming near the bank and wriggling into the grass. Erlang still could not catch him. Seeing a snake darting out with a splash, he recognized it as the Great Sage. He turned around and changed into a gray crane with a cinnabar crest, its long beak like a pointed pair of iron tongs, and came straight to eat this water snake. The water snake sprang once and changed into a spotted báo bird, dull and unadorned, standing on the reed-bank. Erlang saw him become such a base creature—(the hua-bào is among the most vulgar and licentious birds, mating with anything from phoenix, eagle, and raven onward) and so he did not crowd close. He then resumed his original form, strode over, picked up the sling, drew it full, and with one shot knocked him into a backward spin.

The Great Sage seized the chance, rolled down the cliff, hid there, and changed again, becoming an earthen temple: its mouth wide open like a temple gate; teeth became the gate leaves; tongue became a Bodhisattva; eyes became lattice windows. Only the tail was hard to conceal, so he raised it behind him as a flagstaff. True lord arrived at the cliff’s foot, saw no fallen hua-bò bird, only a tiny temple. He quickly opened his wide eyes and looked carefully; seeing the flagstaff behind, he laughed, “So this is the monkey. Once again he’s deceiving me there. I have seen temples before, and never one with a flagstaff standing behind it. Surely this brute is making sport of me. If he lures me in, he’ll bite me in one go. How could I consent to entering? First I’ll knock at the lattice, then I’ll kick the gate leaves.” Hearing this, the Great Sage shuddered in fear: “How fierce, how fierce! The gate leaves are my teeth, the lattice my eyes. If he breaks my teeth and shatters my eyes, what will become of me?” With one tiger leap he sprang and rose into the air, vanishing.

Erlang rushed chaotically before and behind, and only then saw the Four Great Marshals and the two Generals arriving together and flocking around him, saying, “Elder brother, have you caught the Great Sage?” Erlang laughed, “That monkey just changed into a temple to mock me. I was just about to strike his lattice and kick his gate leaves when he jumped and vanished. How strange, how strange!” All were startled, and looking everywhere there was still no trace. Erlang said, “Brothers, stay here and guard patroling this place. I’ll go up and search for him.” He immediately sprang up, rode the clouds, and appeared in midair. He saw Li the Heavenly King raising high the Truth-Revealing Demon Mirror, with Nezha standing beside him in the clouds. Erlang asked, “Great King, have you seen this Monkey King?” Li Tianwang replied, “I have not come up; from here I have been watching him with the mirror.” Erlang then explained all the shape-shifting tricks and the matter of seizing the troop of monkeys. He added, “He turned into a temple and when I was about to strike him, he escaped.” Hearing this, Li Tianwang again swept the mirror in four directions and laughed, “Erlang, go, go quickly. He used a concealment art and slipped out of the encirclement, heading toward your Guanjiao.” Erlang, hearing this, at once took up his divine spear and returned to Guanjiao to pursue.

By this time the Great Sage had reached Guanjiao mouth, transformed himself into the likeness of Erlang, dropped below the cloud bank, and went straight into the temple. The ghost officials could not recognize him and each one bowed in greeting. He sat in the middle and checked the incense accounts: the three sacrificial victims offered by Li Hu, the protection blessing promised by Zhang Long, Zhao Jia’s petition for a son, and the cure vow of Qian Bing. As he was in the middle of this, someone announced, “Another father-elder has come.” The ghost judges hurriedly looked and were all startled. Erlang asked, “Where is the Great Sage who equals Heaven that has just come here?” The ghost judges said, “We have not seen any Great Sage; only one elder is inside checking the incense.” Erlang burst through the temple doorway. The Great Sage saw him and revealed his true form, saying, “Young lord, no need to shout; this temple has already become the surname Sun.” At once this Erlang raised his three-pronged, two-edged divine spear and struck across the face. The Monkey King used a body shift to let the spear pass. He drew out the embroidered pin, flicked it once, and it spread to the breadth of a basin as it rushed forward, meeting him face to face. The two of them shouted and brawled, fought out of the temple, half in mist and half in cloud, fighting while advancing and then returning to Flower-Fruit Mountain. Alarmed, the four Great Heavenly Kings and the rest tightened the defenses still more. Thus the likes of Commander Kang and Commander Zhang received Erlang and, with unified effort, enclosed the handsome Monkey King—details not repeated here.

After Great Force Ghost King had dispatched Erlang and his six brothers to raise troops and arrest the demon, he returned to the upper realm to report. The Jade Emperor, Guanyin Bodhisattva, the Queen Mother, and the host of immortals were in Lingxiao Hall when he said, “Since Erlang has gone to join the battle, there is still no report returned today.” Guanyin joined her palms and said, “Your Majesty, please take the Patriarch of the Way out beyond the South Heavenly Gate and go yourself to see what is real.” The Jade Emperor said, “What you say is reasonable.” He then mounted and, together with the Path-Ancestor, Guanyin, the Queen Mother, and all the immortals, went to the South Heavenly Gate. Some heavenly soldiers and strong attendants were already there to receive them and open the gate for distant observation. They saw heavenly guards setting a net and surrounding all four sides; Li Tianwang and Nezha held up the Demon-Detecting Mirror in the air; in the center Erlang had the Great Sage encircled, and all around them fierce battle was flashing.

The bodhisattva said to the Old Lord, “How is that Erlang Shen you mentioned? If he truly has divine power, he has already surrounded the Great Sage, only he has not yet captured him. I shall now lend him one move and surely seize him.” The Old Lord said, “Bodhisattva, what weapon will you use? How will you help?” The bodhisattva said, “I will throw down the willow from the pure bottle at the monkey’s head. Even if it cannot kill him, it will at least make him take a hard fall so young Erlang may seize him.” The Old Lord said, “Your bottle is porcelain; if it hits him, good. But if it misses his head and strikes his iron staff, will it not shatter? Do not move yet—let this Old Lord lend him one helping strike.” The bodhisattva asked, “What weapon do you have?” The Old Lord said, “I have it, have it, have it.” He rolled up his sleeves and took a ring from his left upper arm and said, “This weapon is made of tempered kun-steel, refined by me with elixir and infused with spirit-qi. It can transform, is not harmed by fire or water, and can ensnare all things. It is called ‘Jin Gang Zuo,’ also called ‘Jin Gang Tao.’ In the old days when I crossed Huan Pass and converted barbarians into Buddha, it proved very useful. Morning and evening it is most useful for self-defense. Let me cast it down and strike him once.”

After speaking, from above the Heavenly Gate he cast it downward in one sweep, and it came dripping through the air, landing squarely on the Monkey King’s head in the Flower-Fruit Mountain encampment. The Monkey King, intent on fighting the seven saints, did not realize a heavenly weapon had fallen. It struck him and, unable to keep his footing, he staggered and fell once. He tried to rise and run, but Erlang’s little hound ran up, bit his thigh, and yanked him for another fall. He fell face-down and cursed, “Wretch! You did not go to trouble my elder at home, yet you come to bite Old Monk!” He tried to scramble up but could not; the seven saints closed in and held him. They bound him with ropes, then drove a hooked blade through the pipa bone, and he could not transform anymore.

Afterward, the Old Lord collected the Jin Gang Zuo and asked the Jade Emperor, Guanyin, Queen Mother, and all immortals to return together to Lingxiao Hall. Below, the Four Great Heavenly Kings and Li Tianwang and his gods all withdrew their forces, pulled up their camps, and came forward to congratulate the young saint, all saying, “This is the merit of this little saint.” The young saint said, “This is all the Buddha’s great blessing and the power of the heavenly deities; what merit is mine?” Kang, Zhang, Yao, and Li said, “Elder brother, no need for many words. Bind this brute and take him to the upper realm to see the Jade Emperor for an edict.” The True Lord said, “Good brother, you have not yet received the heavenly tally and cannot appear before the Jade Emperor. Have the Tianjia soldiers escort him; I will go with the heavenly kings above to report. You four Generals and two commanders should keep your troops here and clear-search the mountain, then return to Guankou. Let me ask for reward and merits, then come back and celebrate together.” The four Grand Commanders and two Generals accepted as told. The True Lord and the hosts then mounted cloud steeds, sang a victory ode, and ascended triumphantly. Soon they came before the Hall of Lingxiao. The Heavenly Master then reported, “The Four Great Heavenly Kings and the others have captured the demon-monkey Qitian Dashi. They are here to await Your Majesty’s judgment.” The Jade Emperor issued an order: “Command Great-force Ghost King and the Heavenly soldiers to take him to the demon-slaying platform and chop this brute to pieces.” Ah! It is exactly as follows:

欺誑今遭刑憲苦，英雄氣概等時休。

In the end, none knows yet how the Monkey King’s life will fare; wait for the next chapter’s unfolding.
chapters.title: Chapter 6: Guanyin attends the celestial gathering to ask why; the young sage shows wondrous might and subdues the Great Sage.

chapters.html:
This is a fresh, complete English translation of Wu Cheng’en’s public-domain one-hundred-chapter novel, produced with GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark assistance. It is an AI-assisted first edition, not a reproduction of an existing translation.

Wealth and rank are settled by former karma; let no one for the sake of being a person ever deceive the heart. Be upright and bright; let loyalty and goodness bear fruit deeply. Every bit of arrogance, when it rises, heaven comes to punish; what is bad in front now must wait until its time arrives. Ask the Lord of the East: why have disasters and calamities closed in now? It is because the heart aimed too high and without limit, not distinguishing upper from lower, upsetting the proper order and all admonitions.

When the Great Sage of Equal Heaven was seized by the heavenly soldiers and taken beneath the altar where demons are slain, they tied him to the demon-subduing pillar, and swords hacked, axes chopped, spears thrust, and sabres cleft—never a hair of him was harmed. Then the Southern Dipper stars ordered the Fire Department gods to burn him, yet even fire could not scorch him. Next they ordered the Thunder Department gods to strike him with thunder-splinters; still he was not even nicked. The Great Demon King and his attendants reported together: “Your Majesty, this brute—who knows from where he learned this body-protection method? I have cut and hacked him with swords and axes; thunder and fire have done nothing. How are we to deal with him?” The Jade Emperor asked, “How can this brute be punished?” The Supreme Elder Lord Lao reported: “This monkey has eaten the peaches of immortality, drunk the celestial wine, and stolen immortal elixirs. My five cauldrons of cinnabar, both raw and ripened, he has swallowed all. Through the use of samādhi fire he has forged his body into a block of gold-stone [gold steel], so it is not easily wounded. Better take him to me and place him in the Eight-Chart Furnace, refine him there with civil and martial fire, and after my elixir is extracted, his body will be reduced to cinders.” The Jade Emperor then ordered the Six-Ding and Six-Jia to unbind him and hand him to the Old Lord. Lao Jun went at once. Elsewhere, Erlang Xiansheng conferred upon him gifts of golden flowers, a hundred jars of imperial wine, one hundred pills of restorative elixir, rare jewel-orbs, and brocade and such things, and told his sworn brothers to share them. The True Lord thanked him and returned to the Guanjiang mouth; no further account is given.

When the Old Lord arrived at Doushita Palace, he untied the Great Sage, removed the pipa-bone restrainer, and thrust him into the Eight-Trigram Furnace. He ordered the Taoist in charge of the furnace and the boys who stoked it to raise the fire and begin tempering him. The furnace was arranged with Qian, Kan, Gen, Zhen, Xun, Li, Kun, and Dui. He placed him exactly under the Xun-trigram seat. Xun is wind: where there is wind, there is no fire. Only that wind stirred the smoke and burned both eyes red to flames, creating a diseased, old sore-eye condition, so it came to be called “Fire-Eye Golden-Pupil.”

Time passed quickly; it was not long before forty-nine days had elapsed. The Old Lord’s tempering was complete. One day he opened the furnace to withdraw the elixir. The Great Sage, with both hands pressing at his eyes, was rubbing and wiping tears, when suddenly he heard the sound at the furnace mouth. He abruptly opened his eyes to the brilliance, could not restrain himself, leapt once, and jumped out of the cauldron, letting out a loud ‘hu-la,’ kicking over the Eight-Trigram Furnace and making straight for the exit. Alarmed, the fire-stokers, furnace-watchers, and the Ding and Jia attendants rushed to pull him, but he knocked them all down one by one, like a white tiger in a seizure, like a wild unicorn-drake in a storm. Lao Jun rushed in to grab him, but the Great Sage jerked him with one pull, flipping him over in a backward somersault and breaking away. Then from his ear he drew out the Ruyi staff, whirled it in the wind; though its width was like a bowl mouth, it remained in his hand, and without regard to right or wrong he again threw the celestial court into chaos, knocking the Nine Luminaries to close doors and shutters and making the Four Heavenly Kings vanish from sight. There is a poem to bear witness, it said:

The true body is rooted in the Primordial Source, for ten thousand kalpas and countless cycles it is simply so. Subtle and formless, all-mixed Great Taiyi; unmoving and unmoved, it is called primal Mystery. Long forged in the furnace, not from lead and cinnabar, life beyond objects is an original immortality. Transforming without end, changing still again and again, all talk of the Three Refuges and Five Precepts is to be set aside. And again: A single spark of spirit-light pierces the Great Void; this staff I hold is of that same nature. At times long, at times short as a man requires, crossing or upright, it winds and uncoils at will. And again: A monkey-bodied Way matches the human heart; in the heart the monkey way is profound. The Great Sage, Equal to Heaven, is not an empty claim; with what can an office of Bi-ma truly understand? Horse and monkey make one heart and one intent, tightly bound and no further search outside. All forms return to true reality from one principle; Tathagata and I abide together in Shuanglin.

In this phase, the Monkey King paid no heed to rank and station, striking east and west with his iron staff. No god in heaven could block him; he only kept advancing to the Hall of Clarity and beyond Lingxiao Hall. By good fortune, Wang Lingguan, the assistant of You Sheng Zhenjun, was stationed there and saw the Great Sage rampaging, so he stepped forth with a golden whip to block him: “Where are you headed, splashed-with-monkey-madness one? As long as I stand here, do not run wild.” The Great Sage gave no reply and struck with his staff. Lingguan snapped out his whip in return. In front of Lingxiao Hall, the two clashed in one place, ferocious combat ensued:

Red-blooded and loyal, upright and righteous, to deceive Heaven and taunt Heaven’s high ones ruins one’s fame. At one time low, at one time high, yet they wrestle on in mutual hold; stalwart heroes contend like gamblers in contest. The iron staff is fierce, the golden whip swift; how can upright fairness endure this? This one is Taiyi Thunder-Voice Responsive and Transforming Lord, that one is the Great Sage of Equal Heaven, monkey demon. Iron whip and iron staff, two houses each with divine and immortal weapons. Today in the Lingxiao Precious Hall they display might and prestige, each truly splendid. One with deceitful mind seeks to seize the Bull-and-Ox palace, one with all his force protects the mysterious holy realm. They quarrel and do not yield, showing divine powers without decisive victory.

The two fought in one place with no winner yet decided. Already, You Sheng Zhenjun again sent orders to the Thunder Court, summoning thirty-six Thunder Generals to gather in haste and surround the Great Sage at the Great Wondrous Center, while each of the troops fought savagely. The Great Sage showed not a trace of fear. With one Ruyi staff he blocked left and right and front and back. At once he saw the thunder gods’ knives, spears, halberds, whips, drums, and hammers, axes, battle-axes, golden melons, sickles, and moon-sickles and shovels coming thickly. He changed his body at once: he became three heads and six arms. He flicked the staff once and made it three; with six hands he extended three staves, like a spinning wheel as it whirls, streaming and circling in the center of the sky-field. No Thunder God could come near. Truly:

Round and complete, shining bright—how can people through the ages learn this? It cannot be burned by fire, nor have it drowned in water. One jewel of light, like a mani pearl, is not harmed by sword, halberd, spear, or blade. He can do good and he can do evil; here and now, good and evil depend on what he does. In goodness he becomes Buddha and becomes an immortal. In evil he grows fur and bears horns. Boundless transformations make trouble through Heaven’s Court; even thunder-god armaments cannot seize him.

At that time the gods packed the Great Sage in one place, but still could not come near him, and they fought in noise and confusion. This at once alarmed the Jade Emperor, who then ordered Youyi Lingguan and Yisheng Zhenjun to go west to request Buddha’s arrival to subdue him.

Receiving the jade edict, the two saints immediately went to the Leiyin Precious Stupa before the exalted realm of Ling Mountain. After bowing to the Four Vajra Kings and Eight Bodhisattvas, they immediately conveyed the matter. The host gods then followed down to the base of the Pearl-Lotus Terrace and announced, “Buddha summons you.” The two circled the Buddha three times and stood below the terrace. Buddha asked, “For what matter from the Jade Emperor has brought you to trouble me?” They replied: “At one time a monkey was born on Huaguo Mountain. There he performed sorcery, gathered hordes of monkeys, and disturbed the world. The Jade Emperor issued an imperial recall, bestowed on him the title Bima-wen to pacify him; he despised the office as too low and rebelled. Li Tianwang and Prince Nezha were sent to capture him but failed. He was then invited again and made Great Sage Equal to Heaven, with office but no stipend at first. He was appointed to oversee the Peach Garden and promptly stole the peaches. He also went to the Jade Pool Court, stole delicacies and wine, disrupted the great assembly; drunk, he slipped into Doushui Palace, stole Lao Jun’s immortal elixir, and came out of Heaven. The Jade Emperor again sent ten thousand heavenly soldiers, and still he could not be subdued. Later, at Guanyin’s request, he was chased by Erlang True Lord as his sworn elder-brother. He constantly changed form; only after Lao Jun threw the golden-steel mallet at him and struck him was Erlang finally able to seize him. Brought before the throne, he was ordered to be beheaded, cut by sword and axe, burned and thunderstruck, yet none could injure him. Lao Jun petitioned and was allowed to take him for tempering by fire. Forty-nine days later the furnace was opened; yet he again leapt out of the Eight-Pattern Crucible, drove off the heavenly officers, and directly entered the Hall of Clarity, outside Lingxiao Hall. At the threshold, the aide of You-sheng Zhenjun, Wang Lingguan, blocked him and they fought bitterly; then the thirty-six thunder generals trapped him in the heart of the field, yet he could not be approached. As the matter was urgent, the Jade Emperor especially invited Buddha to come for rescue.” On hearing this, Buddha told the assembly, “You all sit steadily in this Dharma hall and do not disturb this meditation seat. I will go to subdue the demon and save this matter.”

Buddha summoned the two elders A-ha and Kashyapa to accompany him, left Leiyin, and came straight to the outside of Lingxiao Gate. Suddenly a cry resounded in the air: the thirty-six thunder generals were surrounding the Great Sage. Buddha’s Dharma command was sent: “Tell the thunder generals to cease hostilities, open their ranks, and call out the Great Sage to come forth so I may ask him what powers he has.” They all withdrew. The Great Sage withdrew his illusory form and appeared in his true form before Buddha, angrily fierce, crying out, “Who are you, good holy man, to dare to stop this sword-and-spear fighting and question me?” Buddha smiled, “I am Śākyamuni Buddha of the Western Pure Land of Amitabha. Namo Amitabha Buddha! I have heard you, from the start, have been unruly and wild, repeatedly defying Heaven and returning to it. I do not know from which region you were born, in what year you attained the Way, and why you are so violent.” The Great Sage answered:

In heaven and earth, my spirit was formed from the primal mix, a single old ape in Flower-Fruit Mountain. At Water Curtain Cave I made my home, and seeking masters with sworn companions, I awakened the Great Mystery. I forged long-life arts in many kinds, learned transformations vast and boundless. Since in the mortal realm the land was narrow to me, I resolved in my heart to dwell in Jade Heaven. Lingxiao’s Precious Hall is not his alone; through generation after generation, kings have passed down their allotted shares. If the strong are honored, let them yield me way; only a hero dares to contend for primacy. Buddha laughed coldly: “You there, monkey spirit in beast form, dare to harbor such thoughts and seek to usurp the Jade Emperor’s seat? From youth you claim cultivation and have endured one thousand seven hundred fifty kalpas. Every kalpa is one hundred twenty-nine thousand six hundred years; tell me how many years you say this gives you to enjoy the boundless Great Way. As for this beastly life that began as human, how can you speak so high? You are no child of man, no child of man at all—preserve your years. Submit at once and cease this nonsense. Otherwise deadly harm may come and life will end this instant; pity your original form is wasted.” The Great Sage replied: “Though he has long practiced from youth, he should not occupy it so long. As the saying goes, ‘The emperor’s turn passes round, and next year it comes to my house.’ Merely tell him to move out and give me the celestial hall, then it is enough. If he refuses, there will be endless uproar and no peace.” Buddha said, “Apart from longevity arts and transformation, what else do you have to dare seize Heaven’s realm?” The Great Sage said: “My methods are many: I have seventy-two transformations; my life does not age for myriad kalpas; I can ride the jingu cloud and in one leap go a distance of 108,000 li. How could I not sit in the seat of Heaven?” Buddha said, “Let us wager. If you can hurl yourself out of my right hand with one jingu-cloud leap, then you win and need not use weapons again; I will ask the Jade Emperor to move westward and reside in the west, and give this heaven palace to you. If you cannot strike out of my palm, return to the lower world as a demon, practice for some kalpas more, and come back to quarrel.” The Great Sage laughed to himself: “This Buddha is easy to fool. My jingu cloud goes one leap of 108,000 li; his right palm is not even a foot across. How could I not get out?” he cried, “Then make such a proposition?” Buddha said, “Yes, yes,” and spread out his right hand, which seemed to be only the size of a lotus leaf.

The Great Sage put down the Ruyi staff, gathered his divine might, and with one leap stood in Buddha’s palm, saying, “I will go out as well.” In one line of cloud-light he was gone, no form and no shadow. Buddha used his wisdom-eye and saw that the monkey king resembled a windmill-like thing, never still, always moving forward. As he advanced, suddenly he saw five red, flesh-colored columns, propping up a stream of green-blue qi. “This is the end of the road,” he thought. “When I return, Buddha will bear witness—Lingxiao Palace is surely where I will sit.” Then he thought, “Wait, I’ll leave a mark, then I can speak with Buddha about what happened.” He pulled out one fine hair, blew a trace of immortals’ breath, and cried, “Transform!” It became a thick black two-tipped brush. On the middle column he wrote one line: “Great Sage Equal to Heaven, I visited here.” Having done so, he gathered back the hair and, without concern, urinated once at the base of the first column. Then he flipped his jingu cloud and returned directly to where he had been, standing in Buddha’s palm and saying, “I have gone and now I am back. Instruct the Jade Emperor to give him the Heavenly Palace.”

Buddha scolded, “You urine-spirit monkey, you truly have not even left my palm.” The Great Sage said, “You know nothing.
